Basics of Gas Submetering
What Is a Gas Sub-Meter?

A gas sub-meter is a device that measures the consumption of natural gas for a particular unit in a building. It is installed between the main gas meter and the individual unit, allowing for accurate measurement and billing of gas consumption. Gas submetering is a fair and transparent way of billing tenants for the natural gas they use, as they are only charged for their individual usage.
Benefits of Submetering for Tenants and Property Owners

Submetering has several benefits for both tenants and property owners. For tenants, submetering promotes fairness and transparency in billing, as they are only charged for the natural gas they use, rather than a portion of the building's overall gas bill. This can lead to significant cost savings for tenants, especially in buildings with uneven gas usage.

For property owners, submetering can lead to increased energy efficiency and lower operating costs. By accurately measuring gas usage, property owners can identify areas of high usage and take steps to reduce consumption. This can lead to lower energy bills and reduced carbon emissions.

Installation and Setup

Gas submeters are an effective way to monitor gas usage in multi-family buildings and commercial properties. Installing a gas submeter can help you reduce energy consumption, lower operating costs, and increase property value. In this section, we'll cover the key factors to consider when choosing and installing a gas submeter, as well as the overall installation process.
Choosing the Right Gas Submeter

When choosing a gas submeter, it's important to consider the specific needs of your property. Factors such as the size of the building, number of units, and gas usage patterns should all be taken into account. At Axis Meter Solutions, we offer a range of gas submeters to suit different property types and sizes. Our submeters are designed to be easy to install and maintain, with high accuracy and reliability.
Installation Process Overview
The installation process for a gas submeter typically involves the following steps:
Site survey: A site survey is conducted to assess the property and determine the best location for the gas submeter.
Meter installation: The gas submeter is installed in the chosen location, typically near the gas supply line.
Wiring: Wiring is run from the gas submeter to the utility room or other central location where the data will be collected.
Data collection: Data is collected from the gas submeter and transmitted to a central system for monitoring and analysis.

At Axis Meter Solutions, we have a team of experienced technicians who can handle every aspect of the installation process. We work quickly and efficiently to minimize disruption to your tenants and ensure that the installation is completed on time and on budget.

In general, retrofitting an existing building with a gas submeter is likely to be more expensive than installing a submeter in a new construction project. Reading and Billing

If you're a property owner or manager who has installed gas sub meters, you need to understand how to read the meters and ensure accurate billing. This section will cover the basics of meter readings and billing, as well as the allocation of utility costs.
Understanding Meter Readings

Gas sub meters measure the amount of gas used by individual tenants. Meter readings can be taken manually or automatically, depending on the type of meter installed. Manual readings require someone to physically read the meter and record the usage. Automatic readings are taken electronically and sent to a central system for processing.

To read a gas sub meter manually, you need to locate the meter and record the current reading. The reading will be displayed on the meter in cubic feet or cubic meters. You can then subtract the previous reading from the current reading to determine the amount of gas used since the last reading.
Ensuring Accurate Billing

Accurate billing is essential for both property owners and tenants. Property owners need to ensure that they are billing tenants correctly, while tenants want to make sure they are only paying for the gas they use. To ensure accurate billing, it's important to keep track of meter readings and use a reliable billing system.

At Axis Meter Solutions, we specialize in sub-metering for a diverse range of real estate investments. Our team of experts can help you manage your gas sub meters and ensure accurate billing for all tenants. We use advanced technology to track meter readings and generate accurate bills, so you can focus on managing your property.
Allocation of Utility Costs

Gas sub meters allow for the allocation of utility costs to individual tenants based on their usage. This means that tenants are only responsible for the gas they use, rather than paying a flat rate for utilities. Allocating utility costs can help reduce overall costs for property owners and ensure that tenants are only paying for what they use.

At Axis Meter Solutions, we can help you allocate utility costs and ensure that tenants are only paying for the gas they use. Our metrics include a 32% average property value increase, 18% lower operating costs, and we're 100% regulatory compliant. Trust us to help you manage your gas sub meters and allocate utility costs fairly and accurately.
Technical Specifications
Pulse Output and Its Importance

Pulse output is a feature of gas sub-meters that allows for the measurement of gas consumption by generating a pulse for every unit of gas consumed. The pulse output can be used to track gas usage and also to integrate the meter with data acquisition and billing systems. Pulse output is an important feature for gas sub-meters as it enables more accurate and efficient monitoring of gas consumption.

At Axis Meter Solutions, we understand the importance of pulse output and offer gas sub-meters with pulse output functionality. Our gas sub-meters are designed to deliver superior customer satisfaction and reduce costs by offering measurement accuracy for sub-metering applications.
Capacity and Limitations

The capacity of a gas sub-meter refers to the maximum amount of gas that can be measured by the meter. The capacity of a gas sub-meter is typically measured in cubic feet per hour (cfh). For example, the Leviton GMP10-251 gas sub-meter has a capacity of 250 cfh.

It is important to note that gas sub-meters have limitations. For instance, they may not be suitable for measuring gas consumption in high-pressure applications. It is important to choose the right gas sub-meter for your specific application to ensure accurate measurement and billing.

Our gas sub-meters are designed to meet the specific needs of our clients and are 100% regulatory compliant. Our metrics include a 32% average property value increase and 18% lower operating costs. Choose Axis Meter Solutions for all your utility management needs.
Maintenance and Safety

Gas submeters require routine maintenance to ensure accurate billing and optimal performance. Safety is also a major concern when dealing with gas submeters. In this section, we will discuss routine maintenance for gas submeters and safety protocols and best practices.
Routine Maintenance for Gas Submeters

Routine maintenance on gas submeters is crucial to ensure that they remain fully operational and accurately measure gas consumption. Maintenance activities may include inspection, calibration, and repair. Gas submeter maintenance companies, such as Axis Meter Solutions, provide comprehensive maintenance services to ensure the optimal performance of your submeters.

Axis Meter Solutions is a specialist in sub-metering for a diverse range of real estate investments. They provide routine inspections, proactive repairs, and other maintenance services to preserve the integrity of your utility meters. With Axis Meter Solutions, you can expect an average property value increase of 32%, lower operating costs by 18%, and 100% regulatory compliance.
Safety Protocols and Best Practices

Safety is a top priority when dealing with gas submeters. Accurate metering can serve as an early warning system for potential leaks or faults by detecting unusual spikes or patterns in gas usage. If you prioritize the safety and comfort of building occupants, accurate gas metering products are your best friend.
To ensure safety, it is important to follow safety protocols and best practices. Here are some tips:
Regularly inspect gas submeters for signs of damage or leaks
Train personnel on proper handling and maintenance of gas submeters
Ensure that gas submeters are installed in well-ventilated areas
Use appropriate personal protective equipment when handling gas submeters
Follow all local and national regulations and codes regarding gas submeter installation and maintenance
By following these safety protocols and best practices, you can ensure the safety of your building occupants and prevent costly accidents.

In summary, routine maintenance and safety protocols are crucial when dealing with gas submeters.
